captureMetadata.source: Notion Visual Language Diagram Types database
captureMetadata.privacy: Public-safe snapshot. Notion record IDs, URLs, workspace structure, and private links are omitted.
captureMetadata.scope: Adjacent diagram taxonomy reference used to make support, fidelity, and warning boundaries inspectable.

records.purpose: Models workflows with concurrency (fork/join), decisions, and swim lanes. UML equivalent of flowchart.
records.notes: Flowchart covers most but lacks fork/join bars.
records.commonShapes: Initial node (filled circle), Final node (bullseye), Action (rounded rect), Decision (diamond), Fork/Join (thick bar)

records.purpose: Model enterprise architecture layers and relationships.
records.definition: A formal EA modeling language with specified element types, relationships, and viewpoints.
records.notes: Allow architecture emulations but never claim ArchiMate compliance.
records.commonShapes: Application/service components, business actors, technology nodes, relationships

records.purpose: Formal enterprise architecture modeling language covering business, application, technology, strategy, motivation, and implementation layers.
records.notes: High-value but more complex than BPMN for Mermaid grammar contribution. Good candidate for emulation examples and gap documentation. Primary roles: Enterprise Architect, Solution Architect.
records.originBegan: Developed in the 2000s; ArchiMate 1.0 became an Open Group standard in 2009.
records.domainSpecificity: Enterprise architecture and operating model planning.
records.regionSpecificity: Global, especially common in formal EA practices and organizations using The Open Group standards.
records.commonShapes: Actors, roles, business processes, application components, services, nodes, devices, artifacts, goals, requirements.

records.purpose: Open Group standard for enterprise architecture covering business, application, and technology layers.
records.notes: Complex metamodel. Would need significant custom shapes.
records.commonShapes: Business Actor/Process, Application Component, Technology Node, Serving/Triggering/Flow relationships

records.purpose: Communicate system architecture and boundaries.
records.definition: A diagram showing components/systems and their relationships, typically at multiple abstraction levels.
records.notes: Architecture diagram syntax may be new/beta; renderer differences likely. Keep capability registry warnings.
records.commonShapes: Systems, services, boundaries, links

records.purpose: Represents step-by-step process, decision paths, simple workflows, or cause-effect movement.
records.notes: Primary support target for Mermaid Theme Builder. Highest theming control via classDef, linkStyle, subgraphs, and theme variables. Primary roles: Business Analyst, Process Architect, Developer, Solution Architect, Technical Writer, Operations.
records.originBegan: Industrial engineering lineage; common since early/mid 20th century.
records.commonShapes: Rectangles, diamonds, arrows, terminators, documents, databases, subgraphs.

records.purpose: High-level system decomposition into modules/blocks.
records.definition: A schematic-style decomposition showing major components and their connections at a high level.
records.notes: May be renderer/version dependent (beta syntax); include warnings where needed.
records.commonShapes: Blocks, labeled connectors/lines

records.purpose: ISO/IEC 19510 standard for modeling business processes. Richer than flowcharts with events, gateways, pools, message flows, and artifacts.
records.notes: MAJOR GAP. Millions of practitioners. No text-diagram tool covers it well.
records.commonShapes: Start/End events (circles), Tasks (rounded rectangles), Gateways (diamonds with markers), Pools/Lanes, Message flows (dashed), Data objects

records.purpose: Formal business process modeling notation for end-to-end workflows, orchestration, choreography, events, gateways, pools, lanes, message flows, and automation handoff.
records.mermaidClosestMatch: flowchart, stateDiagram, sequenceDiagram for partial approximations only.
records.notes: Highest-leverage gap candidate. Mermaid flowcharts can imitate simple BPMN-like flows, but they do not implement BPMN semantics. Primary roles: Business Analyst, Process Architect, Enterprise Architect, Solution Architect, Operations.
records.originBegan: BPMI early 2000s; BPMN 1.0 published in 2004; adopted by OMG; BPMN 2.0 finalized around 2010-2011.
records.domainSpecificity: Business process management, workflow automation, process mining, operations, enterprise architecture.
records.regionSpecificity: Global; common in enterprise, consulting, automation, and regulated process work.
records.commonShapes: Events, activities, gateways, pools, lanes, message flows, data objects, annotations.

records.purpose: Standardized business process modeling with executable semantics.
records.definition: A formal process modeling notation (ISO 19510) using standardized events, gateways, tasks, and pools/lanes.
records.notes: Highest-leverage gap. V1: BPMN-lite emulation + warnings. Treat true BPMN as upstream research lane.
records.commonShapes: Start/end events, intermediate events, tasks, gateways, pools/lanes, message flows

records.purpose: Communicate software architecture at multiple abstraction levels (Context/Container/Component/Code).
records.definition: A model for describing software systems using a small set of diagram types and consistent notation.
records.notes: Treat Mermaid’s C4 support as useful but not full C4 tooling; include notation/semantic warnings.
records.commonShapes: People, systems, containers, components, boundaries

records.purpose: Communicates software architecture at context, container, component, and code levels.
records.mermaidClosestMatch: C4 support exists but should be treated carefully; architecture-beta and flowchart can approximate.
records.notes: High relevance to OverKill Hill and Mermaid Theme Builder audience. Needs clear support-level warnings. Primary roles: Solution Architect, Enterprise Architect, Developer, Technical Writer.
records.originBegan: Popularized by Simon Brown in the 2010s.
records.commonShapes: People, systems, containers, components, boundaries, relationships.

records.purpose: Four-level abstraction for software architecture. Context, Container, Component, and Code levels.
records.notes: Mermaid added C4 support. Strong alignment.
records.commonShapes: Person (stick figure), Software System (box), Container (box with tech tag), Component (box with type tag)

records.purpose: Root cause analysis. Horizontal spine arrow with diagonal branches for cause categories (6Ms: Materials, Methods, Manpower, Machines, Measurements, Mother Nature).
records.notes: Very common in quality. Distinctive visual not representable in flowchart.
records.commonShapes: Horizontal spine arrow, Diagonal category branches, Sub-cause twigs, Effect box (head)

records.purpose: Model classes, attributes, relationships.
records.definition: UML-like structural diagram of classes/interfaces and their relationships.
records.notes: Keep legibility high; warn about renderer differences in arrowheads if needed.
records.commonShapes: Class boxes, compartments, associations, inheritance arrows

records.purpose: Shows classes, attributes, operations, and relationships (inheritance, association, composition, aggregation). Backbone of OO design.
records.commonShapes: Class box (3-compartment), Association line, Aggregation (open diamond), Composition (filled diamond), Inheritance (triangle arrow), Multiplicity labels

records.purpose: Shows object interactions by spatial layout with numbered messages.
records.notes: Sequence diagrams dominate this space.
records.commonShapes: Object (rect), Link (line), Numbered message (arrow on link)

records.purpose: Shows software components, interfaces (provided/required), and dependencies.
records.notes: C4 covers the concept.
records.commonShapes: Component box (tab icon), Lollipop interface, Socket interface, Dependency arrow, Port

records.purpose: Shows internal structure of a class/component including parts, ports, connectors.
records.notes: Niche even in UML circles.
records.commonShapes: Classifier box, Part (rect inside), Port (small square), Connector line

records.purpose: Model movement of data between processes, stores, and external entities.
records.definition: A DFD shows how data moves through a system via processes, data stores, and external entities.
records.notes: Useful for threat modeling but not a validated security artifact; pair with Threat Model DFD warnings.
records.commonShapes: External entities, processes, data stores, data flows

records.purpose: Shows how data moves through a system. Distinguishes processes, data stores, external entities, and data flows.
records.notes: Common in STRIDE threat modeling. Distinct semantics from flowchart.
records.commonShapes: Process (circle), Data store (open rectangle), External entity (square), Data flow (labeled arrow)

records.purpose: Hierarchical branching diagram for classification, risk analysis, and decision support.
records.notes: Flowchart handles topology; lacks probability annotations.
records.commonShapes: Decision node (rect/diamond), Chance node (circle), End node (triangle), Branches with probabilities

records.purpose: Represent branching decisions and outcomes.
records.definition: A tree structure that models decision points leading to outcomes and leaf results.
records.notes: Common and easy to emulate well; keep it in example library candidates if it earns a file.
records.commonShapes: Decision nodes, branches, outcomes/leaves

records.purpose: Maps software artifacts to physical/virtual infrastructure nodes.
records.notes: Mermaid architecture diagram covers infrastructure.
records.commonShapes: Node (3D box), Artifact (doc icon), Communication path, Execution environment

records.purpose: Model entities/tables and their relationships.
records.definition: A data model diagram showing entities and relationships (often crow’s foot).
records.notes: Mermaid ER syntax is limited vs full ER notations; label as Mermaid-native.
records.commonShapes: Entities/tables, attributes, relationship connectors

records.purpose: Shows entities, attributes, and relationships. Foundational for database design. Notations: Chen, Crow's Foot, IDEF1X.
records.notes: Mermaid uses Crow's Foot notation.
records.commonShapes: Entity (rectangle), Attribute (oval/column), Relationship (diamond/line), Cardinality markers (1, M, 0..1)

records.purpose: ARIS framework notation alternating between events and functions connected by logical operators.
records.notes: Niche but persistent in SAP-heavy orgs.
records.commonShapes: Event (hexagon), Function (rounded rect), Logical operators (AND/OR/XOR circles), Org unit

records.purpose: Represents entities, attributes, relationships, and cardinality in data models.
records.notes: Important example family. Theming needs to respect ER-specific syntax and not over-apply flowchart classDef assumptions. Primary roles: Data Architect, Data Analyst, Developer, Solution Architect.
records.originBegan: Peter Chen published the entity-relationship model in 1976; crow's foot notation later became common in database modeling.
records.domainSpecificity: Database design, data architecture, analytics, software engineering.
records.commonShapes: Entities, relationship lines, cardinality markers, attributes.

records.purpose: Top-down deductive failure analysis using Boolean logic gates tracing to root causes.
records.notes: Specialized. Needs custom AND/OR gate shapes.
records.commonShapes: Top event (rect), Basic event (circle), Undeveloped event (diamond), AND/OR gates, Transfer triangle

records.purpose: General-purpose node/edge diagrams for processes, systems, and logic flows.
records.definition: A directed graph diagram using boxes/nodes and arrows/edges to show steps, decisions, and flow.
records.notes: Primary workhorse; use for many emulations. Keep renderer-safety notes for ELK/links if used.
records.commonShapes: Process box, decision diamond, terminator, connectors, arrows

records.purpose: Visual representation of a process using standardized symbols connected by arrows. The foundational diagram type for nearly all visual process modeling.
records.notes: Mermaid flagship. The workhorse diagram type.
records.commonShapes: Terminator (oval), Process (rectangle), Decision (diamond), Data I/O (parallelogram), Connector (circle), Arrow

records.purpose: Plan and communicate timelines, tasks, dependencies.
records.definition: A project schedule chart showing tasks across time with start/end dates.
records.notes: Theming mostly via themeVariables; keep readability; date parsing varies by renderer.
records.commonShapes: Tasks/bars, sections, milestones, dates

records.purpose: Horizontal bar chart showing tasks, durations, dependencies, and milestones plotted against a calendar timeline.
records.commonShapes: Task bars, Milestone (diamond), Dependency arrows, Critical path highlighting, Sections/groups

records.purpose: Show Git branching/merging history.
records.definition: A visualization of commits and branches over time, showing merges and divergence.
records.notes: Renderer support varies; keep warnings minimal but honest if behavior differs.
records.commonShapes: Commits, branches, merge points

records.purpose: Activity diagram where nodes are interaction fragments (sequence diagrams).
records.notes: Extremely niche.
records.commonShapes: Frame (containing sequence fragment), Decision node, Fork/Join, Initial/Final

records.purpose: Root-cause analysis by causal categories leading into an observed problem.
records.mermaidClosestMatch: ishikawa / fishbone support in Mermaid 11.x line.
records.notes: Excellent showcase of new Mermaid capability and high relevance to visual reasoning. Primary roles: Business Analyst, Operations, Process Architect, Data Analyst.
records.originBegan: Popularized by Kaoru Ishikawa in the 1960s quality movement.
records.domainSpecificity: Quality, Lean, Six Sigma, operations, incident review.
records.regionSpecificity: Global; roots in Japanese quality practices.
records.commonShapes: Main spine, cause ribs, sub-causes, effect/problem head.

records.purpose: Root-cause analysis by categorizing causes.
records.definition: A cause-and-effect diagram with a spine and branching cause categories.
records.notes: High-value emulation: maintain strong warning about not being notation-perfect; prioritize legibility.
records.commonShapes: Spine, ribs/branches, cause labels

records.purpose: Visualize work items across workflow stages.
records.definition: A board organized by status columns, representing workflow progression.
records.notes: Mermaid kanban support can be renderer-dependent; keep warnings and fallback guidance.
records.commonShapes: Columns, cards/items

records.purpose: Radial diagram with a central concept branching into related topics. Used for brainstorming, note-taking, knowledge organization.
records.commonShapes: Central node (large), Branch nodes (decreasing size), Color-coded branches, Curved connecting lines

records.purpose: Capture hierarchical decomposition of ideas/topics.
records.definition: A radial or tree-like hierarchy showing parent/child relationships between concepts.
records.notes: Theme impact is mostly typography and node styling; keep contrast strong.
records.commonShapes: Nodes, branches, levels

records.purpose: Shows physical/logical layout of network devices and connections.
records.notes: Mermaid architecture diagram is new but covers basics.
records.commonShapes: Router, Switch, Firewall, Server, Cloud, WAN link, VLAN boundary

records.purpose: Snapshot of object instances and relationships at a specific moment.
records.notes: Can approximate with classDiagram.
records.commonShapes: Object box (name:Class underlined, attribute values), Links

records.purpose: Show alignment between objectives and key results across levels/owners.
records.definition: A visualization of objectives and key results and how they connect across teams/levels.
records.notes: Treat as visual alignment aid; Mermaid cannot validate OKR semantics (ownership/weights/scoring).
records.commonShapes: Objectives, key results, links/edges, ownership labels, scoring/weights (optional)

records.purpose: Show reporting structure and team hierarchy.
records.definition: A hierarchical diagram of roles/people/teams and reporting lines.
records.notes: Emulation is fine for clarity; not a live HR system-of-record. Avoid personal data in examples.
records.commonShapes: Person/role boxes, reporting lines

records.purpose: Hierarchical tree showing reporting relationships, departments, and positions within an organization.
records.notes: Universal need. Everyone has one. Flowchart TD can approximate but lacks native org chart semantics.
records.commonShapes: Position box (name, title), Reporting lines (solid), Dotted-line reporting (dashed)

records.purpose: Groups model elements into packages showing dependencies and containment.
records.commonShapes: Package (tabbed folder), Dependency arrow (dashed), Import/Access stereotypes

records.purpose: Represent packet structures / protocol payload fields.
records.definition: A diagram showing a packet/frame layout as fields with sizes and labels.
records.notes: Renderer/version dependent; treat as beta-ish. Keep theme expectations conservative.
records.commonShapes: Field boxes, bit/byte ranges, headers/payload sections

records.purpose: Show part-to-whole composition.
records.definition: A circular chart partitioned into slices representing proportions.
records.notes: Limited semantic styling; prioritize label contrast.
records.commonShapes: Slices/labels

records.purpose: Extends UML metaclasses with stereotypes for domain-specific modeling.
records.notes: Meta-level. Not user-facing in practice.
records.commonShapes: Stereotype (guillemet), Extension arrow, Metaclass reference

records.purpose: Map items across two axes (2x2).
records.definition: A scatter/placement diagram in four quadrants based on two dimensions.
records.notes: Check renderer support/version; may require warnings if inconsistent.
records.commonShapes: Axes, quadrant labels, plotted items

records.purpose: Compare items across multiple dimensions (spokes).
records.definition: A multi-axis chart where values are plotted along radial spokes.
records.notes: Often renderer/version dependent; keep warnings and fallback to XY chart if needed.
records.commonShapes: Spokes, polygon areas, labels

records.purpose: Capture requirements and relationships/traceability.
records.definition: A requirement model diagram showing requirement nodes and links between them.
records.notes: Often unfamiliar; include capability/explanation panel in app. Renderer support varies.
records.commonShapes: Requirement boxes, relationships, containment

records.purpose: Show flow distribution (inputs → outputs) with weighted links.
records.definition: A flow diagram where link width encodes magnitude.
records.notes: Theme surface limited; focus on color and label contrast.
records.commonShapes: Nodes, weighted links

records.purpose: Shows time-ordered interactions between actors, systems, services, APIs, or components.
records.notes: Important, but styling surface is narrower than flowchart. Use themeVariables and metadata comments; avoid flowchart-only classDef assumptions. Primary roles: Developer, Solution Architect, Enterprise Architect, Technical Writer.
records.originBegan: UML-era formalization in the 1990s; interaction diagrams existed earlier in software modeling.
records.domainSpecificity: Software engineering, API design, integration architecture.
records.commonShapes: Participants, actors, lifelines, messages, activations, loops, alt/opt blocks, notes.

records.purpose: Show time-ordered interactions between actors/services.
records.definition: A message sequence over time showing participants and ordered calls/responses.
records.notes: Styling surface narrower than flowchart; focus on themeVariables + readable contrast.
records.commonShapes: Actors/participants, lifelines, messages, activation bars

records.purpose: Shows time-ordered message exchanges between objects/actors. Lifelines run vertically; messages are horizontal arrows.
records.notes: One of Mermaid's strongest implementations.
records.commonShapes: Lifeline (dashed vertical), Synchronous message (solid arrow), Async message (open arrow), Return (dashed), Activation bar, Combined fragments (alt, loop, opt, par)

records.purpose: Maps customer actions, frontstage interactions, backstage actions, support processes, and evidence across a service experience.
records.notes: Adjacent to journey maps, useful for example library, but not highest immediate leverage. Primary roles: UX Designer, Product Manager, Business Analyst, Operations.
records.originBegan: Service design lineage; Lynn Shostack introduced service blueprinting in the 1980s.
records.domainSpecificity: Service design, customer experience, operations, product discovery.
records.commonShapes: Swimlanes, touchpoints, stages, evidence, frontstage/backstage lines, support processes.

records.purpose: Map service delivery across customer touchpoints and backstage processes.
records.definition: A service design diagram showing frontstage/backstage actions, support processes, and evidence across time.
records.notes: Useful emulation; include explicit blueprint-convention warning (line of visibility semantics not enforced).
records.commonShapes: Swimlanes, line of visibility, touchpoints, backstage/support steps

records.purpose: High-level process summary: Suppliers, Inputs, Process, Outputs, Customers.
records.notes: More structured table than diagram.
records.commonShapes: 5-column table or linear flow with labeled boxes

records.purpose: Describe state transitions and lifecycle behavior.
records.definition: A state machine diagram with states and transitions triggered by events/conditions.
records.notes: Use for lifecycle governance examples; avoid over-claiming SysML.
records.commonShapes: States, transitions, start/end markers, forks/joins

records.purpose: Shows states of an object and transitions triggered by events. Supports nested states, concurrent regions, history states.
records.commonShapes: State (rounded rectangle), Initial state (filled circle), Final state (bullseye), Transition arrow, Composite state (nested)

records.purpose: Flowchart partitioned into parallel lanes representing different actors, departments, or systems.
records.notes: Emulatable with subgraphs but lacks true lane semantics.
records.commonShapes: Horizontal/vertical lanes, standard flowchart shapes, handoff arrows crossing lanes

records.purpose: Systems modeling language for requirements, structure, behavior, parametrics, and system interactions.
records.mermaidClosestMatch: requirementDiagram, block, classDiagram, stateDiagram, sequenceDiagram partial fragments.
records.notes: Valuable but likely outside current Mermaid Theme Builder scope. More specialized than BPMN. Primary roles: Systems Engineer, Solution Architect, Enterprise Architect.
records.domainSpecificity: Systems engineering, aerospace, defense, embedded systems, complex product engineering.
records.regionSpecificity: Global but strongest in engineering-heavy organizations.
records.commonShapes: Blocks, requirements, ports, activities, states, sequences, parametric constraints.

records.purpose: Model systems requirements/behavior/structure (systems engineering).
records.definition: A formal modeling language related to UML for systems engineering with multiple diagram types and semantics.
records.notes: Mermaid can approximate pieces (state/class/requirements) but is not SysML-compliant.
records.commonShapes: Blocks, states, activities, requirements, parametrics

records.purpose: Threat model using DFD structure + trust boundaries + STRIDE prompts.
records.definition: A threat modeling diagram that uses DFD-like flows plus trust boundaries and security annotations to reason about threats.
records.mermaidClosestMatch: Flowchart with explicit trust boundary subgraphs + labeled flows
records.notes: Mermaid does not validate boundaries or STRIDE coverage; include strong warning language in capability panel/example header.
records.commonShapes: Processes, data stores, external entities, flows, trust boundaries

records.purpose: Shows system components, trust boundaries, data flows, and potential threats for security threat modeling.
records.notes: DFD-based with security annotations. Growing demand with DevSecOps.
records.commonShapes: Process (circle), Data store (parallel lines), External entity (rectangle), Data flow (arrow), Trust boundary (dashed border)

records.purpose: Show events across time (narrative chronology).
records.definition: A chronological sequence of events or milestones placed along time.
records.notes: Renderer support/version can vary; treat as generic-only theming.
records.commonShapes: Events, dates, labels

records.purpose: Shows state changes along a time axis for real-time systems.
records.notes: Better served by WaveDrom.
records.commonShapes: Lifeline with state timeline, Time axis, State change markers, Duration constraints

records.purpose: Show hierarchical composition as nested rectangles.
records.definition: A space-filling visualization where rectangle area represents magnitude within a hierarchy.
records.notes: Renderer/version dependent; treat as beta-ish with warnings.
records.commonShapes: Nested rectangles, labels

records.purpose: Show hierarchical tree structures in a compact form.
records.definition: A hierarchical tree visualization oriented for quick scanning of nested items.
records.notes: Often renderer/version dependent; ensure example works in target renderer set.
records.commonShapes: Indented nodes, branches

records.purpose: Shows actors and their interactions with system use cases. High-level functional requirements visualization.
records.notes: Core UML. Very common in requirements engineering. Surprisingly absent from Mermaid.
records.commonShapes: Actor (stick figure), Use case (oval), System boundary (rectangle), Include/Extend relationships (dashed arrows)

records.purpose: Show user steps and experience over a journey.
records.definition: A staged journey visualization of tasks/steps and qualitative notes/metrics.
records.notes: Styling is limited; focus on typography/contrast. Consider renderer-dependent warnings if needed.
records.commonShapes: Stages, steps, annotations, scores

records.purpose: Lean diagram showing material and information flow, wait states, cycle time, inventory, and waste.
records.mermaidClosestMatch: flowchart can approximate simple value streams, but lacks formal VSM semantics.
records.notes: Valuable gap, but more visual/operations-specific. Better as emulation example before any new grammar effort. Primary roles: Operations, Process Architect, Business Analyst, Executive / Strategy.
records.originBegan: Toyota Production System / Lean lineage; widely popularized in Lean literature in the late 20th century.
records.domainSpecificity: Lean, manufacturing, operations, supply chain, process improvement.
records.regionSpecificity: Global; roots in Japanese Lean manufacturing.
records.commonShapes: Process boxes, inventory triangles, data boxes, timelines, information flow arrows.

records.purpose: Lean value-stream analysis (material/info flow, lead time).
records.definition: A lean method diagram mapping process steps plus inventories, delays, and information flow to compute lead time/value-add.
records.notes: Emulation can be useful, but do not claim standard VSM symbol compliance or calculations.
records.commonShapes: Process boxes, inventory triangles, data boxes, push/pull arrows, timelines

records.purpose: Lean diagram showing material/information flow from supplier to customer with process metrics at each step.
records.notes: Unique visual language. Would require custom shapes.
records.commonShapes: Process box with data box, Inventory triangle, Push/Pull arrows, Electronic info flow (zigzag), Timeline, Kaizen burst

records.purpose: Show set overlap and relationships.
records.definition: A diagram of overlapping sets representing intersections and unions conceptually.
records.notes: If Mermaid gains native Venn, migrate; until then treat as emulation/gap doc.
records.commonShapes: Overlapping circles, labels

records.purpose: Overlapping circles showing set relationships (union, intersection, difference). Extended to Euler diagrams.
records.notes: Universally recognized. Surprisingly absent from text-diagram tools.
records.commonShapes: Circles (2-5 sets), Overlap regions, Labels per region

records.purpose: Strategic landscape map plotting components by visibility (y-axis) and evolution stage (x-axis: Genesis > Custom > Product > Commodity).
records.notes: SHIPPED in Mermaid v11.14.0 (April 2026). Was a top-5 gap, now native. wardley-beta syntax. Mark Craddock implemented: Langium grammar, D3.js renderer, 12 E2E tests, OWM coordinate compatibility. 147 real-world maps validated. Theme Builder needs: detector update, example file, capability registry entry.
records.domainSpecificity: Universal (strong in UK tech, government digital)
records.commonShapes: Component dots, Value chain links (vertical), Evolution axis (horizontal), Inertia markers

records.purpose: Plot values across X/Y axes (line/scatter).
records.definition: A quantitative chart mapping values onto two axes, often as a line series.
records.notes: Check version/renderer support. Keep warnings if inconsistent.
records.commonShapes: Axes, series, points/lines

records.purpose: Describe code-like sequence flows and control logic.
records.definition: A textual DSL for expressing sequence-like behavior that renders as a diagram.
records.notes: Often renderer-dependent; treat as beta-ish with warnings.
records.commonShapes: Participants, messages, control blocks
